lesson.title: Antidepressants: Adjusting the Chemistry Behind Mood
lesson.summary: Antidepressants are a class of psychotropic medication most often used to treat major depressive disorder by altering neurotransmitter activity, most commonly the availability of serotonin, though exactly how this relieves depression is still not fully understood.
lesson.body:
Antidepressants are the class of psychotropic medication most closely associated with treating major depressive disorder, though as noted in the overview of psychotropic medications, some are also prescribed for anxiety-related conditions.

The most commonly prescribed class today is selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, or SSRIs, which work by blocking the reabsorption, or reuptake, of serotonin back into the neuron that released it, leaving more serotonin available at the synapse. Older classes of antidepressants, including tricyclic antidepressants and monoamine oxidase inhibitors, work through different mechanisms and are prescribed less often today, generally because newer medications tend to have more manageable side effect profiles for most people, though older classes are still used in certain cases.

It is tempting to conclude from how SSRIs work that depression is simply caused by having too little serotonin, but researchers have increasingly cautioned that this is an oversimplification. The relationship between serotonin and depression appears to be considerably more complex than a straightforward deficiency, and exactly why increasing serotonin availability relieves depressive symptoms for many people, often only after several weeks of consistent use even though the neurotransmitter change itself happens much faster, is still not completely understood.

This delay between the immediate biochemical effect and the more gradual improvement in mood is one of the more puzzling and actively researched aspects of antidepressant treatment. It is part of why many researchers suspect these medications work partly through slower, longer-term changes in brain circuits, not simply through the immediate shift in neurotransmitter availability.

This chapter describes how antidepressants are generally understood to work as a class of treatment. It is not meant to describe how any individual should evaluate whether medication is appropriate for them, which is a decision made together with a qualified medical professional.
